title: GPU margin provisioning and KV-cache resilience for continuous batching
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Goal: Define and implement a practical margin-provisioning strategy that keeps multi-tenant continuous-batching serving stable under real traffic while maximizing usable weight/KV/activation capacity. This ticket covers design, simulator experiments, telemetry hooks, and a staged rollout plan for an adaptive soft-reserve system and KV-cache resilience features.

Background: We've seen transient OOMs and degraded tail latency in mixed workloads when continuous batching combines with large KV footprints. Prior work (see ENG-314159 and ENG-880001) explored headroom concepts and soft quotas; this ticket operationalizes those ideas into a deployable policy.

Core proposal:
- Runtime-level margin provisioning: compute per-device and per-tenant margin budgets using a moving percentile of observed working set (weights + kv + activations) with an additional "hedging" multiplier for burst variance. The percentile and hedge are configurable per class (low-latency vs background).
- Soft reserves: create ephemeral soft-reserve allocations that can be borrowed/backfilled. Soft reserves behave like a grace slab: when pressure approaches the percentile threshold we enter a graceful throttle window instead of an instant eviction/OOM.
- Prefix-aware KV compaction: implement a KV compaction signal that deallocates or compresses stale prefixes (LRU by prefix + score) ahead of eviction, prioritizing low-hit-rate prefixes.
- Weight shadowing & quantize-fallback: for devices under sustained pressure, shadow older weight copies in compressed (4-bit/8-bit) representations to free activation/KV headroom; this triggers as a last-resort before global throttling.
- Eviction & throttle policy: combine soft-reserve exhaustion, compaction outcomes, and per-tenant SLA classification to decide: (1) attempt compaction, (2) spill small activations to host (if available), (3) degrade batch concurrency for low-priority tenants, (4) as a final step, discard stale KV entries.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Simulator shows >90% reduction in transient OOMs across synthetic mixed workloads compared to current baseline.
2) Tail latency (p99) regression <5% for P0 tenants after rollout on canary devices.
3) Telemetry surfaces a new memory-safety index and soft-reserve burn rate; alerts if burn rate > 80% for > 30s.
4) Feature flag gated rollout and roll-back plan exists with clear runbook steps.

Deliverables & implementation plan:
- Design doc (Confluence): /confluence/redwood/serving/gpu-margin-provisioning (draft ready)
- Simulator changes: extend the memory-sim harness to model prefix-aware KV and soft-reserve semantics (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/memory-sim/pull/73). Run three histograms of per-tenant allocation over 10k simulated minutes.
- Runtime: add a margin manager component that exposes an RPC for current margin and recommended throttle. Implement prefix compaction hook and compressed-weight shadowing prototype behind flags.
- Telemetry: new metrics -- memory_safety_index, soft_reserve_burn, kv_compaction_rate, prefix_hit_rate. Add dashboards in Grafana and a short alert playbook.
- Tests: unit tests for compactor; stress e2e on ci-stress cluster, and a small-scale canary on dedicated pool.

Progress updates:
- 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Serving and Infra (notes linked in Confluence). Agreed to baseline on existing sim harness instead of building a new one.
- 2025-02-18: Simulator prototype merged (PR #70); early runs show soft-reserve reduces OOM spikes but increases tail by ~6% in worst-case synthetic bursts.
- 2025-02-24: Design review with PM/RE to tune hedging multiplier; requested explicit SLA tiers so throttle policy can respect tenant priorities.
- 2025-03-01: Runtime API sketched and discussed in arch sync. Li to implement margin manager interface and initial compaction hook.

Open decisions & trade-offs:
- Hedge sizing: conservative (higher hedge) reduces OOM risk but wastes headroom. We will expose percentile and multiplier as per-project knobs and default to 95th percentile + 1.15 multiplier for mixed workloads.
- Compaction cost vs latency: prefix compaction can add CPU cost and small pauses; we will prioritize low-latency tenants and only compact on sustained pressure windows.
- Host spill vs eviction: host spill reduces immediate OOM risk but complicates scheduling; enable only when host resources available and for short-lived activations.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flagged library + sim validated in staging.
2) Canary on 5% of devices (non-critical tenants) for 2 weeks, monitor memory_safety_index and p99.
3) Gradual expansion to Dedicated pools with nightly automated rollbacks if soft_reserve_burn > 90% for > 5 min.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: compaction adds CPU pressure -> mitigation: measure compaction CPU in sim and cap compaction rate per device.
- Risk: wrong defaults lead to headroom waste -> mitigation: telemetry + canary and smooth ramp.

Review requests & next steps:
- Engineering review (runtime API): @Priya Shah, @Owen Martinez.
- PM review for SLA mapping: @Nina Park.
- Deliver simulator runs for three customer-like workloads (short-chatty, long-context, bursty-reranking) by 2025-03-10.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence design draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/GPU+Margin+Provisioning+Draft
- Simulator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/memory-sim/pull/70
- Runtime API sketch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2168 (WIP)
- Grafana dashboard prototype: grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-margin/soft-reserve-monitor

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on deployable, incremental changes (soft-reserve + compaction + telemetry) rather than a full rewrite of the allocator. The aim is to reduce service-impacting OOMs while preserving batching efficiency for the majority of workloads.
